scope_boundaries: For biased walks, normalize the transition convention in every source (bias toward root vs away, parent weight vs child weight); thresholds and monotonicity parameters cannot be compared until conventions are translated.

Keep transience, positive speed, zero speed/sub-ballistic trapping, harmonic measure existence, and harmonic-measure dimension as distinct claims with their own offspring, leaf, and moment assumptions.
Speed monotonicity results do not imply monotonicity of harmonic-measure Hausdorff dimension; the latter is the target for B076.

Compare harmonic measures only after fixing the underlying boundary, visual metric, conditioning, and quenched/annealed law. Dimension comparison is not by itself a general statement of measure equivalence.

Covering-time, point-process, Euclidean stochastic-geometry, and Galton-Watson boundary measures are different models; shared words such as route, tree, or harmonic measure do not establish a theorem transfer.

SIRSN route-length statements require the stated stationarity, scale invariance, route uniqueness, finite expected route-length and integrability conditions; do not infer a maximum over a countable route family from one sampled route. M0100 is a typical close Poisson-pair variable, not a global maximum; M0109 Mecke identities count points/pairs but do not bound path maxima.

PZ2008CLT assumes a leafless GW tree and toward-root parent weight; BAFGH2012LEAVES assumes p0>0 and away-root bias in the sub-ballistic regime. Curien–Le Gall concerns critical finite-radius GW exit measures and a CRT boundary, not the infinite supercritical biased-walk boundary.

Newly read RWRE papers use iid child-to-parent environment ratios, not the deterministic parent-weight λ or childward β walk; their trajectory maxima, regeneration-time tails, and speed results are separate from harmonic measure and from group-graph dead-end transfer.
